Hi Lina — thanks for sending this over and for the clear asks. Looping in Karthik (legal) and Vanessa (partnerships) to scope response.

Quick context from our side: the integration will be a connector deployed on Redwood-hosted infra (hosted option) with an option for Dedicated later. That drives a couple of standard guardrails we expect to see in the DPA and SOW. To keep the sync efficient, our initial checklist:

- Confirm data flows and whether HorizonVault will be a controller or processor for any customer data.
- Subprocessor notification & approval process.
- Retention and deletion timelines (we typically ask 30 days for customer data post-termination; logs retained 90 days unless otherwise agreed).
- SLA language and measurable acceptance criteria in SOW (uptime, API latency targets, incident MTTR).
- Liability cap guidance — we often default to 3x ACV or $2M (whichever is higher) for integrations like this; we can be flexible in negotiation.

Can you share your preferred times on Tue/Wed after 1pm PT? I'm attaching our internal partner-redlines-tracker.csv so everyone can mark priorities.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: HorizonVault x Redwood: Integration MSA/DPA + SOW redlines

Monica / Lina — thanks for the context. I reviewed HorizonVault_MSA_redline_v1.docx and the DPA supplement and here are Redwood's high‑level positions (so we can narrow items prior to a sync):

1) Limitation of Liability: our standard position for partner integrations of this nature is a cap equal to the greater of (i) 3x fees paid in the prior 12 months, or (ii) $2,000,000. We can discuss carveouts for gross negligence or willful misconduct.

2) Indemnity: we will accept an indemnity limited to third‑party claims arising from partner defects in their connector code or breaches of their data obligations. We cannot accept broad customer indemnities that cover Redwood's own service design.

3) Data Processing / DPA: we need explicit subprocessors notice and a 30‑day cure period before any termination for alleged noncompliance. Encryption at rest and in transit must be documented; we will require a list of primary subprocessors and an SLA for patching security critical vulnerabilities.

4) Audit Rights: Redwood will accept scoped audit rights limited to security controls relevant to the connector (not full business audits). We prefer ISAE/SOC reports in lieu of on‑site audits where available.

5) Data return/deletion: Redwood will delete or return customer data within 30 days post‑termination except for backups/log retention (90 days) unless otherwise agreed.

6) SOW: we need measurable acceptance criteria (endpoints, throughput, sample test plan) and a clearly defined support escalation path and SLA (recommended: 99.9% API availability for production endpoints; 1 hour P1 response).

7) Choice of law: Redwood proposes CA law; we are generally open to negotiation but avoid foreign jurisdictions for commercial deals.

I prepared a redline (Redwood_response_redlines.docx) with inline edits and comments. If HorizonVault is comfortable with the above, we can fast‑track execution. Otherwise flag the top 3 items you want to prioritize in the meeting.

Happy to join a 30 minute call — my availability Wed 2–4pm PT.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Counsel, Commercial & Procurement
Redwood Inference
